The main components of a steam turbine include the rotor, stator, blades, and bearings. The rotor is the rotating part of the turbine, which is connected to the generator to produce electricity. The stator is the stationary part of the turbine, which directs the steam flow into the rotor. The blades are attached to the rotor and rotate at high speeds to extract energy from the steam. The bearings support the rotor and allow it to rotate smoothly.

Failures in steam turbines can occur due to various reasons such as wear and tear, corrosion, fatigue, and overloading. These failures can be classified into two types: incipient failures and abrupt failures.

Incipient failures are those that occur gradually over time and can be detected through the analysis of sensor data. These failures can be caused by factors such as wear and tear, corrosion, and fatigue. In the early stages of an incipient failure, the sensor data may show a slight deviation from the normal operating pattern. For example, there may be a slight increase in the vibration levels, a decrease in the efficiency, or an increase in the temperature. As the failure progresses, the sensor data patterns will become more pronounced, and the deviation from the normal operating pattern will become more significant.

Abrupt failures, on the other hand, are those that occur suddenly and can be caused by factors such as overloading, loss of lubrication, or mechanical failure.
